description:
Multiple public constructors and pure query functions in the in-scope files are missing #[must_use]. Clippy pedantic (must_use_candidate) flags all of these:

pkix-path/src/lib.rs:
- TrustAnchor::new() (line 352) — constructor
- TrustAnchor::from_cert() (line 382) — constructor
- ValidationPolicy::new() (line 557) — constructor
- names_match() (line 1080) — pure predicate used in security checks

pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:
- CertPool::new() (line 52) — constructor
- CertPool::len() (line 62) — pure query
- CertPool::is_empty() (line 67) — pure query
- build_path() (line 223) — main API function returning Result<Vec<_>>

pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs:
- web_pki_policy() (line 89) — factory returning ValidationPolicy
- smime_policy() (line 127) — factory returning ValidationPolicy
- code_signing_policy() (line 159) — factory returning ValidationPolicy
- rfc5280_policy() (line 176) — factory returning ValidationPolicy

Missing #[must_use] on constructors means the compiler will not warn if a caller writes TrustAnchor::new(name, spki); (discarding the result), which is almost certainly a bug. This is especially important on security-critical types like TrustAnchor and on policy factories where discarding the returned policy means no policy is applied.
title: Public constructors and pure functions missing #[must_use]
